title: SPROUTS FARMERS MARKET
intro: At Meaningful Works, the client I have worked with the most has been Sprouts Farmers Market. My work with Sprouts Farmers Market emphasizes the handmade and quirky spirit of the brand. I've been fortunate to create OOH design, in-store displays, art direct and create assets for campaigns, and even create animated social posts. This page displays some work created for Sprouts Farmers Market. Creative Directors: Summer Woodward and Hunter Somerville Design assistance: Kristy Toyoda, Chantal Herrera, Jamie Back, Spencer Fraye Photography: Jason Travis

title: CORITA ART CENTER
intro: In the Fall of 2024, I was fortunate enough to be hired as a Gallery Assistant at Corita Art Center. While I originally helped with various tasks, my role evolved into creating graphic assets for the organization. This involved everything from social posts, to signage, to children's' educational worksheets. My proudest work is "break bread", a zine created for a Corita Art Center benefit dinner. The design for the zine was inspired from the "irregular bulletin", a student-made newsletter that was created during Corita Kent's tenure at Immaculate Heart College.

title: SoCAL EARTH
intro: SoCal Earth is a brand and visual identity project created for the Robert Redford Conservancy for Southern California Sustainability at Pitzer College. SoCal Earth is a new environmental data website and educational program. My role with SoCal Earth was to create its visual identity and enhance its brand. When interviewing the Robert Redford Conservancy, the concept of living off what we already have kept emerging. With this resourceful philosophy in mind, I used the paper I already had in my studio to create the logo. Illustrations, animations, and even a cartoon mascot were all created with paper in my studio and then digitally converted to use on the site. For the final SoCal Earth experience, visit the site here .

title: VALLEY STRONG CREDIT UNION
intro: During my time at Meaningful Works, I've had the opportunity to work on multiple projects for Valley Strong Credit Union. The largest of these projects was creating a visual identity for Valley Strong's home loan program. Valley Strong wanted to reinforce the ease of their program and address anxieties of the home lending process. To address this, we created an identity that focused around a "roof over your head". The visual identity was designed to convey domestic comfort and excite home owners about what's possible with a new home. Creative Director: Summer Woodward Copywriter: Dana Tiel Design assistance: Chantal Herrera

title: THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY
intro: From January to June 2025, I served as a Graphic Design intern with Yellow Shoes at The Walt Disney Company. Yellow Shoes acts as Disney's in-house advertising agency for Disney Experiences and National Geographic Expeditions. Due to Disney's wide scope of businesses and brands, I've been able to create design work for Walt Disney World, Disney Resorts Collection, Downtown Disney, National Geographic Expeditions, and other sectors under Disney Experiences. In addition to print advertising and marketing, I've also created style guides, designed logos, expanded existing brands, and create logo animations. Group Design Director: Agnete Oernsholt Design Director: Lacye Beauregard

title: CULTURAL OLYMPIAD POSTER
intro: In Spring of 2024, the cities of Paris, France and Los Angeles announced a poster competition for the Paris 2024 and Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic games. The invitation to compete was given to three Los Angeles-area schools (ArtCenter College of Design, CalArts, and Otis College of Art and Design) and one Paris-based school (EPSAA: École Professionnelle Supérieure d'Arts graphiques de la Ville de Paris). Students were tasked to create a poster and social media animation that celebrated the Olympic and Paralympic games being held in Paris 2024 and the transition to Los Angeles 2028. Using my love of analog design, I created cut paper designs of the Eiffel Tower, an Olympic torch, and an Academy Award; symbols of the cities and the Olympic games. I'm happy say that my work was one of the entries chosen by the cites of Paris and Los Angeles. My work and other winning posters were displayed along the Canal Saint-Martin in Paris and on the City of Paris's website and social media for the 2024 games. The posters will then be displayed again in 2028 for the Los Angeles games. This project was also given a student bronze from the World Brand Design Society.

title: FORCED PERSPECTIVE
intro: Forced Perspective: An Exhibit On Brand is a thesis and art project about the influence of branding on the public. When studying brands in ArtCenter, I became frustrated by the manipulation and forced judgement of others that comes from some branding practices. To reveal these practices to the public, I created artwork that focused on judgement and perceptions caused by particular brands. The artwork was displayed in a gallery space called The Trophy Room LA for a total of three days in March of 2024. The art, my reflections on branding, and my largest takeaways from the project were all compiled in a 300 page book at the end of the project.

title: CALIFORNIA STATE PARKS
intro: California State Parks is a rebranding project of the entire state organization, one focused on the concept of reclaiming. When researching for the rebrand, I found that California State Parks is an organization frequented mostly by suburban and rural white male audiences. This left younger audiences feeling excluded or “othered” by the current brand. My solution to this feeling of exclusion was to visually reclaim the organization. I created illustrations and found photographs of old California and flooded these with vibrant colors and quirky cartoons. This reclaiming was akin to a type of graffiti, adding a youthful and artistic tone over a serious and outdated identity. California State Parks served as an opportunity to explore a brighter and more cheerful side of branding and implement my illustration skills as well.

title: THE TRADE SHOW!
intro: What's more black and white than money and profit? This is the question I tease in the design of THE TRADE SHOW! This project is a mock museum catalog of artists who focus on consumerism and capitalism in their work. The artist catalog was curated to feature Alex Da Corte, Daniel Arsham, Minerva Cuevas, Tyler Shields, Stephanie H. Shih, Nick Doyle, Jeff Koons, and Barbara Kruger; all are artists who focus on corporate influence in some way. The catalog also contains an essay by Frederic Jameson called “Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism”. THE TRADE SHOW! is a way for me to share my humorous voice as a designer while creating a uniquely blunt commentary on capitalism. THE TRADE SHOW! also won an honorable mention for Graphis's New Talent Awards 2024.

title: KDI
intro: Kounkuey Design Initiative (KDI) is a design nonprofit that focuses on urban and community design for under-resourced groups. In the summer of 2022, I was fortunate to be a graphic design intern with KDI in their Los Angeles office. KDI brought me on to revise, refresh, and expand their existing brand. While I could not change the logo, I was able to create a new visual identity and brand guidelines. Some of the assets created for KDI included a new color palette, logos for individual offices, various documents and templates, graphic icons and illustrations, and a visual code for individual projects. KDI's internship allowed me to gain practical design and branding experience with a fantastic organization.

title: 10 BY TEN ENTERTAINMENT
intro: 10 By Ten Entertainment is a startup production company founded by Hollywood producer Tendo Nagenda. 10 By Ten Entertainment is focusing on telling stories from new and typically underrepresented perspectives, something that interested me greatly. In the summer of 2023, Tendo offered me a summer graphic design intern position at his new company. 10 By Ten Entertainment needed a brand created, along with templates, stationery, a brand bible, and various other assets needed to get the company running. The visuals of the brand were inspired from the short film "Powers of Ten", as this was one of the largest inspirations for the company's name and ideals. My internship with 10 By Ten Entertainment allowed me to be part of a startup company and create a brand from the ground up.

title: BIG TECH ART
intro: Big Tech Art is a 64-page newspaper that critiques art and illustrations used by large tech corporations. The publication contains several online articles that talk about an art style known as "Corporate Memphis". Corporate Memphis is an overly simplistic illustration style that can be found on many large websites. It's used primarily because of its gleeful and simple design and can sometimes be used to mask the wrongdoings of tech companies. As the newspaper progresses, the design becomes more chaotic, reflecting the annoyance of seeing these illustrations over and over again.

title: NOBODY CARES
intro: NOBODY CARES is a short photographic essay which shows our collective indifference to unhoused people. During the summer of 2022, I had an internship in downtown Los Angeles. My walk to the office had many unhoused people along the way, many of which were clearly battling mental health problems. What was disturbing was not the unhoused people, but the other commuters who tried to ignore their existence. Disturbed by this, I started to photograph Angelenos actively ignoring unhoused people. The best photographs were compiled into this book and was self-published on Amazon. A portion of the proceeds from this book will go to local Los Angeles homeless agencies.
